title: Moments, Friction and Inclined Planes
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Maths: Moments and Friction Worksheets
standard_text: Understand and use moments in simple static contexts; resolve forces in two dimensions; understand and use the F ≤ μR model for friction and the coefficient of friction; motion on a rough or smooth inclined plane.
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level maths worksheets on moments, resolving forces, friction F ≤ μR and particles on inclined planes. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How it works

The moment of a force about a point = force × perpendicular distance. In equilibrium, clockwise moments = anticlockwise moments and the forces balance.

Friction F ≤ μR. On a slope at θ, the weight has components mg sin θ down the slope and mg cos θ into the slope.

Example

Mass 5 kg on a smooth slope at 30°. Force down the slope?

5 × 9.8 × sin 30°

Answer: 24.5 N

Common mistakes

  • Using the slant distance for a moment.
  • Using sin for the component into the slope.
  • Taking R = mg on a slope.

faq.a: Choose a point, multiply each force by its perpendicular distance from the point, and set clockwise moments equal to anticlockwise moments.

faq.q: What is the coefficient of friction?
faq.a: μ = F/R when friction is at its maximum (limiting equilibrium or sliding).
